#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Installation Script
# Usage:
#   Latest version: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash
#   Specific version: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- <version>
#   Select skills: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | DMTOOLS_SKILLS=jira,github bash
#   Single skill: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- --skill jira
#   CLI skills: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- --skills=jira,github
#   All skills: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- --all-skills
#   Ignore invalid names: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- --skills=jira,unknown --skip-unknown
#   Legacy strict alias: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/epam/dm.ai/main/install | bash -s -- --skills=jira --strict
# Requirements: Java 17+ (will attempt automatic installation on macOS/Linux)

set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
REPO="epam/dm.ai"
MANIFEST_URL="${DMTOOLS_MANIFEST_URL:-https://dmtools.lab.epam.com/cli-manifest.json}"
# Populated by fetch_manifest() when available.
MANIFEST_JSON=""
MANIFEST_BASE_URL=""
INSTALL_DIR="${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.dmtools}"
BIN_DIR="${DMTOOLS_BIN_DIR:-$INSTALL_DIR/bin}"
JAR_PATH="$INSTALL_DIR/dmtools.jar"
SCRIPT_PATH="$BIN_DIR/dmtools"
INSTALLER_ENV_PATH="${DMTOOLS_INSTALLER_ENV_PATH:-$BIN_DIR/dmtools-installer.env}"
RUNTIME_OVERRIDE_ENV_PATH="${DMTOOLS_RUNTIME_ENV_PATH:-$BIN_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env}"
INSTALLED_SKILLS_JSON_PATH="${DMTOOLS_INSTALLED_SKILLS_JSON_PATH:-$INSTALL_DIR/installed-skills.json}"
ENDPOINTS_JSON_PATH="${DMTOOLS_ENDPOINTS_JSON_PATH:-$INSTALL_DIR/endpoints.json}"
AVAILABLE_SKILLS=(
    dmtools jira confluence github gitlab figma teams
    sharepoint ado testrail xray
)
ALWAYS_ON_INTEGRATIONS=(ai cli file kb mermaid)
INSTALLER_SKILLS_WAS_SET=false
INSTALLER_SKILLS_ARG=""
INSTALLER_ALL_SKILLS_WAS_SET=false
INSTALLER_VERSION_ARG=""
INSTALLER_POSITIONAL_ARGS=()
SKILLS_SOURCE="default"
INSTALL_ALL_SKILLS=false
EFFECTIVE_SKILLS=()
INVALID_SKILLS=()
EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS=()
EFFECTIVE_SKILLS_CSV=""
INVALID_SKILLS_CSV=""
EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS_CSV=""
INSTALLER_SKILL_CONFIG_UNCHANGED=false
STRICT_INSTALL_MODE=false
SKIP_UNKNOWN_SKILLS=false

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}$1${NC}"
}

warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $1${NC}"
}

progress() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}$1${NC}"
}

trim_value() {
    local value="$1"
    value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    printf '%s' "$value"
}

strip_optional_quotes() {
    local value
    value=$(trim_value "$1")
    if [ "${#value}" -ge 2 ]; then
        if [[ "$value" == \"*\" && "$value" == *\" ]]; then
            value="${value:1:${#value}-2}"
        elif [[ "$value" == \'*\' && "$value" == *\' ]]; then
            value="${value:1:${#value}-2}"
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s' "$value"
}

to_lower() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
}

join_by_comma() {
    local IFS=","
    printf '%s' "$*"
}

join_by_comma_space() {
    local result=""
    local item
    for item in "$@"; do
        if [ -n "$result" ]; then
            result="$result, "
        fi
        result="$result$item"
    done
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

normalize_csv_set() {
    local raw_csv="$1"
    local values=()
    local token

    IFS=',' read -r -a csv_tokens <<< "$raw_csv"
    for token in "${csv_tokens[@]}"; do
        token=$(to_lower "$(strip_optional_quotes "$token")")
        token=$(trim_value "$token")
        if [ -z "$token" ]; then
            continue
        fi
        append_unique values "$token"
    done

    if [ ${#values[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "${values[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort | paste -sd, -
}

normalize_structured_content() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

read_env_assignment_value() {
    local file_path="$1"
    local key="$2"
    [ -f "$file_path" ] || return 1

    local raw_value
    raw_value=$(sed -n "s/^${key}=//p" "$file_path" | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$raw_value" ] || return 1

    strip_optional_quotes "$raw_value"
}

json_escape() {
    local value="$1"
    value="${value//\\/\\\\}"
    value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
    value="${value//$'\n'/\\n}"
    value="${value//$'\r'/\\r}"
    value="${value//$'\t'/\\t}"
    printf '%s' "$value"
}

json_string_array() {
    local values=("$@")
    local json="["
    local first=true
    local value
    local escaped

    for value in "${values[@]}"; do
        escaped=$(json_escape "$value")
        if [ "$first" = false ]; then
            json+=", "
        fi
        json+="\"$escaped\""
        first=false
    done

    json+="]"
    printf '%s' "$json"
}

json_skill_objects() {
    local values=("$@")
    local json="["
    local first=true
    local value
    local escaped

    for value in "${values[@]}"; do
        escaped=$(json_escape "$value")
        if [ "$first" = false ]; then
            json+=", "
        fi
        json+="{\"name\":\"$escaped\"}"
        first=false
    done

    json+="]"
    printf '%s' "$json"
}

json_endpoint_objects() {
    local values=("$@")
    local json="["
    local first=true
    local value
    local escaped

    for value in "${values[@]}"; do
        escaped=$(json_escape "$value")
        if [ "$first" = false ]; then
            json+=", "
        fi
        json+="{\"name\":\"$escaped\",\"path\":\"/dmtools/$escaped\"}"
        first=false
    done

    json+="]"
    printf '%s' "$json"
}

append_unique() {
    local array_name="$1"
    local candidate="$2"
    eval "local current=(\"\${${array_name}[@]}\")"
    local existing
    for existing in "${current[@]}"; do
        if [ "$existing" = "$candidate" ]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    eval "${array_name}+=(\"\$candidate\")"
}

append_requested_skills_arg() {
    local value
    value=$(strip_optional_quotes "$1")
    value=$(trim_value "$value")
    if [ -z "$value" ]; then
        return 0
    fi

    if [ -n "$INSTALLER_SKILLS_ARG" ]; then
        INSTALLER_SKILLS_ARG="${INSTALLER_SKILLS_ARG},${value}"
    else
        INSTALLER_SKILLS_ARG="$value"
    fi
    INSTALLER_SKILLS_WAS_SET=true
}

is_known_skill() {
    case "$1" in
        dmtools|jira|confluence|github|gitlab|figma|teams|sharepoint|ado|testrail|xray)
            return 0
            ;;
        *)
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
}

append_skill_integrations() {
    local skill="$1"
    case "$skill" in
        jira)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "jira"
            ;;
        confluence)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "confluence"
            ;;
        github)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "github"
            ;;
        gitlab)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "gitlab"
            ;;
        figma)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "figma"
            ;;
        teams)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "teams"
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "teams_auth"
            ;;
        sharepoint)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "sharepoint"
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "teams_auth"
            ;;
        ado)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "ado"
            ;;
        testrail)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "testrail"
            ;;
        xray)
            append_unique EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS "jira_xray"
            ;;
    esac
}

build_effective_integrations() {
    EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS=("${ALWAYS_ON_INTEGRATIONS[@]}")
    local skill
    for skill in "${EFFECTIVE_SKILLS[@]}"; do
        append_skill_integrations "$skill"
    done
    EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS_CSV=$(join_by_comma "${EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATIONS[@]}")
}

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

    echo "Error: Java 17+ is required but not found." >&2
    echo "Please install DMTools first:" >&2
    echo "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Brand colors (teal/cyan theme)
# Detect terminal capabilities and use appropriate color mode
# macOS Terminal often doesn't support 24-bit colors, so we check TERM_PROGRAM
USE_24BIT=false
if [ -n "$COLORTERM" ] && [[ "$COLORTERM" == *"truecolor"* ]]; then
    USE_24BIT=true
elif [ -n "$TERM_PROGRAM" ] && [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" != "Apple_Terminal" ]]; then
    # For non-Apple terminals, check if 256color is supported
    if [ -n "$TERM" ] && [[ "$TERM" == *"256color"* ]]; then
        USE_24BIT=true
    fi
fi

if [ "$USE_24BIT" = true ]; then
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[38;2;102;208;232m'      # #66D0E8 - Light teal
    TEAL_DARK='\033[38;2;51;153;204m'        # #3399CC - Darker blue-green
else
    # Use 256-color palette for better compatibility, or fallback to ANSI
    # For macOS Terminal, use bright cyan which looks good
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[1;36m'                  # Bright cyan (works well in macOS Terminal)
    TEAL_DARK='\033[0;36m'                   # Cyan
fi
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
CYAN_BRIGHT='\033[1;36m'
WHITE='\033[1;37m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else

        # Current working directory (highest priority)

        "dmtools-installer.env"

    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

### BLOCKING
1. **AC1 fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is rejected by the production runtime; `pullRequestID` is the schema casing.**
   - Evidence: dmtools v1.7.256 (exact version installed by `setup/dmtools.sh` for CI/live runs) catalog declares `pullRequestID` required for `github_get_pr_diff_text` AND `github_get_pr_diff`.
   - Live execution against the v1.7.256 jar: `pullRequestId` → `{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}`; `pullRequestID` → success.
   - Repo history: #193 (dc48d6b1) documented exactly this ("Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error") and #201 set `pullRequestID` deliberately.
   - The `typeof github_get_pr_diff_text !== 'undefined'` guard passes (the global exists in GraalJS), the call throws, `getDiffText` catches → returns null; `getPrDiff` catches → falls through to legacy tool (which still has correct `pullRequestID`) → masked again. Net effect: the PR reintroduces the exact 100%-failure-primary-path + fallback-masks-it pattern the ticket set out to fix, on the production runtime.
   - Where the "host callback returned invalid JSON ×4" in run 37806292238 came from: NOT the arg casing (both my local QuickJS 0.1.43 runtime and the schema confirm `pullRequestID` works). The root cause hypothesis was never validated — with a mocked success path (AC2 test), the tests only pin the arg name, they never prove the runtime accepted it.
   - Merging = breaking `getDiffText`/`getPrDiff` primary path in all live runs (pr_review diff truncation, inline comment validation, etc.).

2. Also part of the same finding or separate? The unit tests pin the wrong casing (they'd fail a correct re-fix). I'll fold this into the blocking finding since fixing the casing requires updating the tests.

### IMPORTANT
3. **postTestReviewComments.js:112 calls `github_get_pr_diff` with `pullRequestId`** — the casing the production schema rejects. Latent 100%-failure with silent catch (returns null → inline-comment validation skipped). Pre-existing, outside the diff → general comment. Actually wait, let me re-check: line 109-112 `github_get_pr_diff({ workspace, repository, pullRequestId: String(prNumber) })`. Yes. On the production runtime this fails with "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing", caught → warn → returns null. This is the same class of bug as gh-802's supposed fix — worth flagging in the general comment as follow-up scope (the ticket's non-goals exclude it, but it's directly relevant evidence).

Hmm — should this be inline? It's NOT in the diff (postTestReviewComments.js unchanged) → general comment per rules.

4. **AC3a claim about `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` semantics** — let me double-check: after `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` on an up-to-date branch, git prints "Already up to date." and does NOT modify the index or create MERGE_HEAD. Index == HEAD → `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` exits 0 → "already up to date" branch → correct.
   When the merge stages changes → exit 1 → throw → staged=true → "base branch changes staged" → correct.
   Edge: any OTHER git failure of the quiet-diff (e.g., corrupt index) would be classified "staged changes" — a benign false claim; low risk. I could offer a SUGGESTION to log the quiet-diff error when it's not exit 1... but the `cmd` helper's error message includes the exit code? The mock returns 'COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0' appended output — in the real runtime, `cli_execute_command` throws with the output including COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=N. Can't easily distinguish exit 1 from other failures without parsing. The catch-all → "staged" is the same behavior as before the change (old code always claimed staged). So no regression — fine. No finding needed, maybe a small note. Not worth cluttering.

5. **AC3b — `markReworkInDevelopment` now writes IN_REWORK**: knob name vs. behavior mismatch is intentional per PR (compat). The new comment explains. One question: projects that enabled the knob because their bounce-back is READY_FOR_DEVELOPMENT expected a transition to "In Development" — now they get "In Rework" which might not exist in their Jira workflow → moveToStatus fails → warn (non-fatal). It's opt-in and the failure is caught; the card stays in the queued status. Acceptable behavior change documented in PR. I'd call this a SUGGESTION (mention knob rename opportunity) — actually the PR explicitly says "Knob name unchanged (config compatibility)". Since IN_REWORK is project-overridable via config.jira.statuses, projects without an "In Rework" status can map it. Fine — SUGGESTION-level at most. Actually, is it worth flagging that writing a status that may not exist in some workflows is now the guaranteed outcome for legacy knob users? The failure path is caught and warned. I'll make it a SUGGESTION.

6. **Test AC3c asserting `!passesRawObject`** — the assertion forbids ANY object arg in console.error calls. That's a behavior pin specific to the host console rendering. Fine.

7. Check `getDiffText` — after the inverted fix, on QuickJS 0.1.43 both casings work, so local e2e/dev runs pass; only production Java runs break. This asymmetry is exactly why the wrong fix looked green. Worth stating in the review.

Let me also double-check the claim in the PR description: "The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it." — TRUE per catalog. But then the PR's own logic ("schema declares X → pass X") contradicts itself: the `github_get_pr_diff_text` catalog ALSO declares `pullRequestID`. The author claimed the opposite schema without verifying. This internal inconsistency supports the blocking finding.

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

error() {

    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        "$@" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Load environment variables from various .env files
# Usage: load_env_files [quiet]
#   quiet: if set, don't print info messages
load_env_files() {
    local quiet_mode="${1:-false}"
    local env_files=(
        # Current working directory (highest priority)
        ".env"
        "dmtools.env"
        "dmtools-installer.env"
        "dmtools-local.env"
        # Script directory (lower priority)
        "$[REDACTED:Credential File]"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-installer.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-local.env"
    )
    
    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Load environment files silently (will be reloaded with messages when command is executed)
load_env_files quiet

# Try to find JAR file in multiple locations
find_jar_file() {
    local jar_file=""

    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$install_dir/dmtools.jar" ]; then
            echo "$install_dir/dmtools.jar"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Check local build directory (development)
    if ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    # Check for any JAR file in the script directory
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 \( -name "dmtools*.jar" -o -name "*-all.jar" \) | head -1)
    # Check parent directory build folder (if script is in subdirectory)
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    fi
    
    echo "$jar_file"
}

JAR_FILE=$(find_jar_file)

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Brand colors (teal/cyan theme)
# Detect terminal capabilities and use appropriate color mode
# macOS Terminal often doesn't support 24-bit colors, so we check TERM_PROGRAM
USE_24BIT=false
if [ -n "$COLORTERM" ] && [[ "$COLORTERM" == *"truecolor"* ]]; then
    USE_24BIT=true
elif [ -n "$TERM_PROGRAM" ] && [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" != "Apple_Terminal" ]]; then
    # For non-Apple terminals, check if 256color is supported
    if [ -n "$TERM" ] && [[ "$TERM" == *"256color"* ]]; then
        USE_24BIT=true
    fi
fi

if [ "$USE_24BIT" = true ]; then
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[38;2;102;208;232m'      # #66D0E8 - Light teal
    TEAL_DARK='\033[38;2;51;153;204m'        # #3399CC - Darker blue-green
else
    # Use 256-color palette for better compatibility, or fallback to ANSI
    # For macOS Terminal, use bright cyan which looks good
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[1;36m'                  # Bright cyan (works well in macOS Terminal)
    TEAL_DARK='\033[0;36m'                   # Cyan
fi
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
CYAN_BRIGHT='\033[1;36m'
WHITE='\033[1;37m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        "$@" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Load environment variables from various .env files
# Usage: load_env_files [quiet]
#   quiet: if set, don't print info messages
load_env_files() {
    local quiet_mode="${1:-false}"
    local env_files=(
        # Current working directory (highest priority)
        ".env"
        "dmtools.env"
        "dmtools-installer.env"
        "dmtools-local.env"
        # Script directory (lower priority)
        "$[REDACTED:Credential File]"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-installer.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-local.env"
    )
    
    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Load environment files silently (will be reloaded with messages when command is executed)
load_env_files quiet

# Try to find JAR file in multiple locations
find_jar_file() {
    local jar_file=""

    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$install_dir/dmtools.jar" ]; then
            echo "$install_dir/dmtools.jar"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Check local build directory (development)
    if ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    # Check for any JAR file in the script directory
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 \( -name "dmtools*.jar" -o -name "*-all.jar" \) | head -1)
    # Check parent directory build folder (if script is in subdirectory)
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    fi
    
    echo "$jar_file"
}

JAR_FILE=$(find_jar_file)

🚨 **BLOCKING: The fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is the casing the production runtime REJECTS; `pullRequestID` is the schema-required one**

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

    echo "Please install DMTools first:" >&2
    echo "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Brand colors (teal/cyan theme)
# Detect terminal capabilities and use appropriate color mode
# macOS Terminal often doesn't support 24-bit colors, so we check TERM_PROGRAM
USE_24BIT=false
if [ -n "$COLORTERM" ] && [[ "$COLORTERM" == *"truecolor"* ]]; then
    USE_24BIT=true
elif [ -n "$TERM_PROGRAM" ] && [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" != "Apple_Terminal" ]]; then
    # For non-Apple terminals, check if 256color is supported
    if [ -n "$TERM" ] && [[ "$TERM" == *"256color"* ]]; then
        USE_24BIT=true
    fi
fi

if [ "$USE_24BIT" = true ]; then
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[38;2;102;208;232m'      # #66D0E8 - Light teal
    TEAL_DARK='\033[38;2;51;153;204m'        # #3399CC - Darker blue-green
else
    # Use 256-color palette for better compatibility, or fallback to ANSI
    # For macOS Terminal, use bright cyan which looks good
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[1;36m'                  # Bright cyan (works well in macOS Terminal)
    TEAL_DARK='\033[0;36m'                   # Cyan
fi
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
CYAN_BRIGHT='\033[1;36m'
WHITE='\033[1;37m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        "$@" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Load environment variables from various .env files
# Usage: load_env_files [quiet]
#   quiet: if set, don't print info messages
load_env_files() {
    local quiet_mode="${1:-false}"
    local env_files=(
        # Current working directory (highest priority)
        ".env"
        "dmtools.env"
        "dmtools-installer.env"
        "dmtools-local.env"
        # Script directory (lower priority)
        "$[REDACTED:Credential File]"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-installer.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-local.env"
    )
    
    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Load environment files silently (will be reloaded with messages when command is executed)
load_env_files quiet

# Try to find JAR file in multiple locations
find_jar_file() {
    local jar_file=""

    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$install_dir/dmtools.jar" ]; then
            echo "$install_dir/dmtools.jar"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Check local build directory (development)
    if ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    # Check for any JAR file in the script directory
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 \( -name "dmtools*.jar" -o -name "*-all.jar" \) | head -1)
    # Check parent directory build folder (if script is in subdirectory)
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    fi
    
    echo "$jar_file"
}

JAR_FILE=$(find_jar_file)

        if [ -n "$chosen" ]; then

                target="${chosen#run:}"
                exec "$0" run "$target"
            else
                # chosen is "tool_name\tjson_params\toutput_format"
                tool_name="${chosen%%$'\t'*}"
                rest="${chosen#*$'\t'}"
                params="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
                output_format="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                if [ "$params" = "$rest" ]; then
                    output_format=""

                output_args=()

The production runtime (dmtools **v1.7.256** — the exact version `setup/dmtools.sh` installs) validates the tool schema, and it declares **`pullRequestID`** (required) for `github_get_pr_diff_text`. Reproduced live against the v1.7.256 jar:

```
$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestId": "803"}'
{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}

$ dmtools github_get_pr_diff_text --data '{..., "pullRequestID": "803"}'
{"result": "diff --git a/js/common/gitOps.js ..."}   ← works
```

This repo's own history agrees twice:
- #193 (`dc48d6b1`): *"Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error"* — fixed TO `pullRequestID`.
- #201 (`92aea814`): switched to `github_get_pr_diff_text` keeping `pullRequestID`.

### What merging this does

Both primary diff-text calls (`getDiffText` here and `getPrDiff` at `scm.js:271`) will throw 100% of the time on the production runtime. `getDiffText` returns `null`; `getPrDiff` silently falls through to the legacy `github_get_pr_diff` (stats-only, no usable diff) and then to a **local git diff** — which cannot serve merged PRs with deleted head branches, the exact case the diff-text tool exists for. The fallback chain masks the failure again — the precise pattern this ticket set out to eliminate.

Note dmtools' own catalog is inconsistent: all other `github_*` PR tools take `pullRequestId`, but **both** diff tools take `pullRequestID` — assuming uniform casing is what caused this.

### Root cause of the ticket's evidence was misattributed

The forensic `host callback returned invalid JSON` ×4 in run 37806292238 cannot have been caused by the `pullRequestID` casing (it is the schema casing; both my live executions above prove the tool accepts it). That failure had a different cause (runner's dmtools build, response-envelope parse, or `IS_READ_PULL_REQUEST_DIFF` gating). The new unit tests mock the global, so they pin the intent — they can never validate it against the real host.

### Required fix

1. Revert both call sites to `pullRequestID: String(prId)` / `pullRequestID: prIdStr` (same args as `github_get_pr_diff` at `scm.js:284`, which this PR correctly leaves alone).
2. Re-pin the tests (`test_githubHelpers.js` `pullRequestId` assertions at ~899-903 and ~1414) to `pullRequestID` + keep the AC2 call-count test.
3. Leave a comment on the casing asymmetry so the next agent doesn't "fix" it again.
4. Re-open the gh-802 forensic question separately: re-check run 37806292238's dmtools build before attempting any runtime-behavior change.

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

    echo "Please install DMTools first:" >&2
    echo "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Brand colors (teal/cyan theme)
# Detect terminal capabilities and use appropriate color mode
# macOS Terminal often doesn't support 24-bit colors, so we check TERM_PROGRAM
USE_24BIT=false
if [ -n "$COLORTERM" ] && [[ "$COLORTERM" == *"truecolor"* ]]; then
    USE_24BIT=true
elif [ -n "$TERM_PROGRAM" ] && [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" != "Apple_Terminal" ]]; then
    # For non-Apple terminals, check if 256color is supported
    if [ -n "$TERM" ] && [[ "$TERM" == *"256color"* ]]; then
        USE_24BIT=true
    fi
fi

if [ "$USE_24BIT" = true ]; then
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[38;2;102;208;232m'      # #66D0E8 - Light teal
    TEAL_DARK='\033[38;2;51;153;204m'        # #3399CC - Darker blue-green
else
    # Use 256-color palette for better compatibility, or fallback to ANSI
    # For macOS Terminal, use bright cyan which looks good
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[1;36m'                  # Bright cyan (works well in macOS Terminal)
    TEAL_DARK='\033[0;36m'                   # Cyan
fi
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
CYAN_BRIGHT='\033[1;36m'
WHITE='\033[1;37m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        "$@" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Load environment variables from various .env files
# Usage: load_env_files [quiet]
#   quiet: if set, don't print info messages
load_env_files() {
    local quiet_mode="${1:-false}"
    local env_files=(
        # Current working directory (highest priority)
        ".env"
        "dmtools.env"
        "dmtools-installer.env"
        "dmtools-local.env"
        # Script directory (lower priority)
        "$[REDACTED:Credential File]"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-installer.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-local.env"
    )
    
    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Load environment files silently (will be reloaded with messages when command is executed)
load_env_files quiet

# Try to find JAR file in multiple locations
find_jar_file() {
    local jar_file=""

    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$install_dir/dmtools.jar" ]; then
            echo "$install_dir/dmtools.jar"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Check local build directory (development)
    if ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    # Check for any JAR file in the script directory
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 \( -name "dmtools*.jar" -o -name "*-all.jar" \) | head -1)
    # Check parent directory build folder (if script is in subdirectory)
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    fi
    
    echo "$jar_file"
}

JAR_FILE=$(find_jar_file)

    if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then

        if [ -n "$chosen" ]; then
            if [[ "$chosen" == run:* ]]; then
                target="${chosen#run:}"
                exec "$0" run "$target"
            else
                # chosen is "tool_name\tjson_params\toutput_format"
                tool_name="${chosen%%$'\t'*}"
                rest="${chosen#*$'\t'}"
                params="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
                output_format="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                if [ "$params" = "$rest" ]; then
                    output_format=""
                fi
                output_args=()
                if [ -n "$output_format" ]; then
                    output_args=("--output" "$output_format")
                fi
                if [ -n "$params" ] && [ "$tool_name" != "$params" ]; then
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" --data "$params" "${output_args[@]}"
                else
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" "${output_args[@]}"
                fi
            fi
        fi

                COMMAND="$1"
            else
                ARGS+=("$1")
            fi
            shift
            ;;

done

chosen=$("$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner interactive)
        if [ -n "$chosen" ]; then
            if [[ "$chosen" == run:* ]]; then
                target="${chosen#run:}"
                exec "$0" run "$target"
            else
                tool_name="${chosen%%$'\t'*}"
                rest="${chosen#*$'\t'}"
                params="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
                output_format="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                if [ "$params" = "$rest" ]; then
                    output_format=""
                fi
                output_args=()
                if [ -n "$output_format" ]; then
                    output_args=("--output" "$output_format")
                fi
                if [ -n "$params" ] && [ "$tool_name" != "$params" ]; then
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" --data "$params" "${output_args[@]}"
                else
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" "${output_args[@]}"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        exit 0
        ;;
    "doctor")
        if [ -z "$JAR_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$JAR_FILE" ]; then
            error "DMTools JAR file not found. Please install DMTools first or build the project."
        fi
        "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner doctor
        exit $?
        ;;
    "run")
        # Handle run command with JSON file, JS file, or direct job name + optional encoded parameter
        if [ ${#ARGS[@]} -lt 1 ]; then
            error "Run command requires at least one argument: json-file-path or job-name"
        fi
        
        JSON_FILE="${ARGS[0]}"
        
        # Extra args after ARGS[0] (file) — includes optional encoded param and --key value pairs (e.g. --ciRunUrl)
        EXTRA_RUN_ARGS=("${ARGS[@]:1}")

        info "Executing job with file: $JSON_FILE"
        # Run is not a tool — stderr must NOT be suppressed so errors are visible in CI logs
        "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner run "$JSON_FILE" "${EXTRA_RUN_ARGS[@]}"
        exit $?
        ;;
esac

# Check if JAR file exists
if [ -z "$JAR_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$JAR_FILE" ]; then
    error "DMTools JAR file not found. Please install DMTools first:
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash

Or if you're developing locally, build the project first:
  ./gradlew build

Note: Java 17+ is required for DMTools to run."
fi

# Check if command starts with - or --, then proxy directly to JobRunner
if [[ "$COMMAND" == -* ]]; then
    # Direct proxy to JobRunner for flags like --version, --help, etc.
    CMD_ARGS=("$COMMAND")
    if [ ${#ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        CMD_ARGS+=("${ARGS[@]}")
    fi
    
    # Execute directly without mcp prefix
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner "${CMD_ARGS[@]}"
    else
        "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner "${CMD_ARGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null
    fi
    exit $?
fi

# Proxy all other commands to JobRunner as MCP tools
# Build command arguments array
CMD_ARGS=("$COMMAND")
if [ ${#ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    CMD_ARGS+=("${ARGS[@]}")
fi

# Check if STDIN has data (heredoc/pipe)
if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
    STDIN_DATA=$(cat)
    if [ -n "$STDIN_DATA" ]; then
        [ "$QUIET" = false ] && info "Reading JSON from STDIN (${#STDIN_DATA} characters)"
        CMD_ARGS+=("--stdin-data" "$STDIN_DATA")
    fi
fi

# Add --data or --file flags if provided
if [ -n "$DATA" ]; then
    [ "$QUIET" = false ] && info "Using inline data"
    CMD_ARGS+=("--data" "$DATA")
elif [ -n "$FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
        error "File not found: $FILE"
    fi
    [ "$QUIET" = false ] && info "Using file data: $FILE"
    FILE_DATA=$(cat "$FILE")
    CMD_ARGS+=("--data" "$FILE_DATA")
fi

# Add verbose/debug flags
if [ "$QUIET" = false ]; then
    CMD_ARGS+=("--verbose")
fi
if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
    CMD_ARGS+=("--debug")
fi

# Add output format flag if provided
if [ -n "$OUTPUT_FORMAT" ]; then
    CMD_ARGS+=("--output" "$OUTPUT_FORMAT")
fi

# Execute command via JobRunner as MCP tool
if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
    "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner mcp "${CMD_ARGS[@]}"
else
    "$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j.configuration=$LOG_CONFIG -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner mcp "${CMD_ARGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null
fi

**ABSOLUTELY DECISIVE**: Against the production Java dmtools v1.7.256 runtime (the exact version CI installs per `setup/dmtools.sh`):

- `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `pullRequestId` → **`{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}`** — the call FAILS.
- `github_get_pr_diff_text` with `pullRequestID` → **success**, returns the diff.

So this PR's core fix (AC1) is **backwards**. It changes working code into 100%-broken code on the production runtime. This is a critical BLOCKING finding:

1. The PR's stated root cause is inverted. The tool schema (both in v1.7.256 and the QuickJS 0.1.43 build) requires `pullRequestID`. Commit dc48d6b1 (#193) explicitly documented this: "Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error."
2. The forensic evidence in the ticket ("host callback returned invalid JSON" ×4 with `pullRequestID`) must have had a different root cause (e.g., a transient dmtools bug, response envelope issue, or a different build on that runner) — the arg name was NOT the cause, since `pullRequestID` is the schema casing.
3. Merging this PR would break `getDiffText` and `getPrDiff` primary paths 100% of the time on the production runtime — exactly the failure mode the ticket set out to fix, now guaranteed by the "fix". The fallback chain would again silently mask it.
4. The new unit tests pin the WRONG casing (`pullRequestId`), so the test suite now actively enforces the broken behavior.

Also worth checking: does the QuickJS-native 0.1.43 (the one installed HERE, used for local test runs) accept both? Yes — I verified both casings work there. That explains why the dev machine job passed its tests (mocks anyway) and why the author believed the change worked. But production CI (`setup/dmtools.sh` → Java v1.7.256) validates the schema strictly.

Wait — I should double check which runtime the agents repo's own CI test runs use. The tests run via `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`. In GitHub Actions of THIS repo, dmtools is installed via setup/install.sh dmtools → Java v1.7.256. But do the unit tests call the real tool? No — mocks. So tests pass either way. The breakage manifests only in live agent runs (preJSAction/preCliJSAction of pr_review, rework, etc.).

Let me also verify the other claims of the PR quickly:

- AC3a (gitOps staged-changes log): logic is correct. `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` exit codes: 0 = no diff, 1 = diff. After a no-op merge, index == HEAD → exit 0 → "already up to date". After a real merge, index differs → exit 1 → "staged". Correct. One caveat: `cmd()` throws on non-zero exit (established by the mock and setupCommands). In the REAL runtime, does cli_execute_command throw on non-zero exit code? Let me check how the real cli_execute_command behaves... In gitOps.js the pattern `try { cmd(...) } catch (e)` is used for `git merge` conflict detection — the merge error path is triggered by the throw. So yes, non-zero exits throw. The AC3a change is correct and safe. Also there's a subtle detail: on a conflicted merge, the merge command throws → caught by outer catch → fine.

  Edge: If `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` throws for a reason OTHER than "differs" (e.g., git error), the code would claim "base branch changes staged" — a minor false-positive risk, but pre-existing style. Acceptable.

- AC3b (preCliReworkSetup IN_REWORK): Semantics — the knob is named `markReworkInDevelopment` but now writes `IN_REWORK`. Config compatibility: the knob name is unchanged; the status it writes changes. Is `statuses.IN_REWORK` always defined? `resolveStatuses` provides defaults. Let me check js/config.js for IN_REWORK default and how `statuses` is resolved in preCliReworkSetup.js. Also — wait, the comment says the opt-in is for projects whose bounce-back target is a "queued" status (e.g. READY_FOR_DEVELOPMENT). Previously the transition went queued → In Development. Now it goes queued → In Rework. But what if a project's workflow doesn't HAVE an "In Rework" status? Then `moveToStatus(ticketKey, 'In Rework')` would fail → caught → warn. Pre-existing behavior for failure. But the DEFAULT `statuses` mapping — let me check config.js resolveStatuses to see what IN_REWORK defaults to.

- AC3c (fetchQuestionsToInput error content): correct and matches the host console {} behavior claim. Let me verify the claim about console rendering Error as {}. The comment in the test says "verified in the dmtools GraalJS runtime". Plausible. The fix is fine. Note: `String(fetchError)` in GraalJS would produce "Error: message" — fine.

- AC3d (test-only pin): fine.

Now let me check `statuses` resolution for AC3b.

**Decisive evidence found.** Against the production Java runtime (v1.7.256 — exactly what `setup/dmtools.sh` installs for CI):
- `pullRequestId` → `{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}`
- `pullRequestID` → success, returns the diff

The PR's core fix is inverted. Let me verify the remaining AC3 items before writing the review.

AC3c: fine.

blocks.text:
Confirmed. The tests pin `pullRequestId`, which is the casing the production runtime REJECTS. The unit tests can never catch this because they mock the global.

Now let me compile my complete findings:

### BLOCKING
1. **AC1 fix is inverted — `pullRequestId` is rejected by the production runtime; `pullRequestID` is the schema casing.**
   - Evidence: dmtools v1.7.256 (exact version installed by `setup/dmtools.sh` for CI/live runs) catalog declares `pullRequestID` required for `github_get_pr_diff_text` AND `github_get_pr_diff`.
   - Live execution against the v1.7.256 jar: `pullRequestId` → `{"error": true, "message": "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing"}`; `pullRequestID` → success.
   - Repo history: #193 (dc48d6b1) documented exactly this ("Passing 'pullRequestId' causes a 'Required parameter pullRequestID is missing' error") and #201 set `pullRequestID` deliberately.
   - The `typeof github_get_pr_diff_text !== 'undefined'` guard passes (the global exists in GraalJS), the call throws, `getDiffText` catches → returns null; `getPrDiff` catches → falls through to legacy tool (which still has correct `pullRequestID`) → masked again. Net effect: the PR reintroduces the exact 100%-failure-primary-path + fallback-masks-it pattern the ticket set out to fix, on the production runtime.
   - Where the "host callback returned invalid JSON ×4" in run 37806292238 came from: NOT the arg casing (both my local QuickJS 0.1.43 runtime and the schema confirm `pullRequestID` works). The root cause hypothesis was never validated — with a mocked success path (AC2 test), the tests only pin the arg name, they never prove the runtime accepted it.
   - Merging = breaking `getDiffText`/`getPrDiff` primary path in all live runs (pr_review diff truncation, inline comment validation, etc.).

2. Also part of the same finding or separate? The unit tests pin the wrong casing (they'd fail a correct re-fix). I'll fold this into the blocking finding since fixing the casing requires updating the tests.

### IMPORTANT
3. **postTestReviewComments.js:112 calls `github_get_pr_diff` with `pullRequestId`** — the casing the production schema rejects. Latent 100%-failure with silent catch (returns null → inline-comment validation skipped). Pre-existing, outside the diff → general comment. Actually wait, let me re-check: line 109-112 `github_get_pr_diff({ workspace, repository, pullRequestId: String(prNumber) })`. Yes. On the production runtime this fails with "Required parameter 'pullRequestID' is missing", caught → warn → returns null. This is the same class of bug as gh-802's supposed fix — worth flagging in the general comment as follow-up scope (the ticket's non-goals exclude it, but it's directly relevant evidence).

Hmm — should this be inline? It's NOT in the diff (postTestReviewComments.js unchanged) → general comment per rules.

4. **AC3a claim about `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` semantics** — let me double-check: after `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` on an up-to-date branch, git prints "Already up to date." and does NOT modify the index or create MERGE_HEAD. Index == HEAD → `git diff --cached --quiet HEAD` exits 0 → "already up to date" branch → correct.
   When the merge stages changes → exit 1 → throw → staged=true → "base branch changes staged" → correct.
   Edge: any OTHER git failure of the quiet-diff (e.g., corrupt index) would be classified "staged changes" — a benign false claim; low risk. I could offer a SUGGESTION to log the quiet-diff error when it's not exit 1... but the `cmd` helper's error message includes the exit code? The mock returns 'COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0' appended output — in the real runtime, `cli_execute_command` throws with the output including COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=N. Can't easily distinguish exit 1 from other failures without parsing. The catch-all → "staged" is the same behavior as before the change (old code always claimed staged). So no regression — fine. No finding needed, maybe a small note. Not worth cluttering.

5. **AC3b — `markReworkInDevelopment` now writes IN_REWORK**: knob name vs. behavior mismatch is intentional per PR (compat). The new comment explains. One question: projects that enabled the knob because their bounce-back is READY_FOR_DEVELOPMENT expected a transition to "In Development" — now they get "In Rework" which might not exist in their Jira workflow → moveToStatus fails → warn (non-fatal). It's opt-in and the failure is caught; the card stays in the queued status. Acceptable behavior change documented in PR. I'd call this a SUGGESTION (mention knob rename opportunity) — actually the PR explicitly says "Knob name unchanged (config compatibility)". Since IN_REWORK is project-overridable via config.jira.statuses, projects without an "In Rework" status can map it. Fine — SUGGESTION-level at most. Actually, is it worth flagging that writing a status that may not exist in some workflows is now the guaranteed outcome for legacy knob users? The failure path is caught and warned. I'll make it a SUGGESTION.

6. **Test AC3c asserting `!passesRawObject`** — the assertion forbids ANY object arg in console.error calls. That's a behavior pin specific to the host console rendering. Fine.

7. Check `getDiffText` — after the inverted fix, on QuickJS 0.1.43 both casings work, so local e2e/dev runs pass; only production Java runs break. This asymmetry is exactly why the wrong fix looked green. Worth stating in the review.

Let me also double-check the claim in the PR description: "The legacy `github_get_pr_diff` fallback keeps `pullRequestID` — that tool's catalog schema genuinely uses it." — TRUE per catalog. #!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}

    echo "Error: Java 17+ is required but not found." >&2
    echo "Please install DMTools first:" >&2
    echo "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Brand colors (teal/cyan theme)
# Detect terminal capabilities and use appropriate color mode
# macOS Terminal often doesn't support 24-bit colors, so we check TERM_PROGRAM
USE_24BIT=false
if [ -n "$COLORTERM" ] && [[ "$COLORTERM" == *"truecolor"* ]]; then
    USE_24BIT=true
elif [ -n "$TERM_PROGRAM" ] && [[ "$TERM_PROGRAM" != "Apple_Terminal" ]]; then
    # For non-Apple terminals, check if 256color is supported
    if [ -n "$TERM" ] && [[ "$TERM" == *"256color"* ]]; then
        USE_24BIT=true
    fi
fi

if [ "$USE_24BIT" = true ]; then
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[38;2;102;208;232m'      # #66D0E8 - Light teal
    TEAL_DARK='\033[38;2;51;153;204m'        # #3399CC - Darker blue-green
else
    # Use 256-color palette for better compatibility, or fallback to ANSI
    # For macOS Terminal, use bright cyan which looks good
    TEAL_LIGHT='\033[1;36m'                  # Bright cyan (works well in macOS Terminal)
    TEAL_DARK='\033[0;36m'                   # Cyan
fi
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
CYAN_BRIGHT='\033[1;36m'
WHITE='\033[1;37m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# Helper functions
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}" >&2
}

# Execute java command with proper stderr handling
# Usage: execute_java_command arg1 arg2 ...
execute_java_command() {
    if [ "$DEBUG" = true ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        "$@" 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Load environment variables from various .env files
# Usage: load_env_files [quiet]
#   quiet: if set, don't print info messages
load_env_files() {
    local quiet_mode="${1:-false}"
    local env_files=(
        # Current working directory (highest priority)
        ".env"
        "dmtools.env"
        "dmtools-installer.env"
        "dmtools-local.env"
        # Script directory (lower priority)
        "$[REDACTED:Credential File]"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-installer.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-runtime.env"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/dmtools-local.env"
    )
    
    for env_file in "${env_files[@]}"; do
        if [ -f "$env_file" ] && [ -r "$env_file" ]; then
            # Check file permissions for security (should not be world-readable for sensitive data)
            if [ -f "$env_file" ]; then
                # Load the environment file, ignoring comments and empty lines
                while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                    # Skip empty lines and comments
                    if [[ -n "$line" && ! "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then
                        # Export the variable if it's in KEY=VALUE format
                        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
                            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                            # Remove surrounding quotes if present
                            value=$(echo "$value" | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//")
                            export "$key"="$value"
                        fi
                    fi
                done < "$env_file"
                if [ "$quiet_mode" != "quiet" ]; then
                    info "Loaded environment variables from: $env_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
}

# Load environment files silently (will be reloaded with messages when command is executed)
load_env_files quiet

# Try to find JAR file in multiple locations
find_jar_file() {
    local jar_file=""

    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$install_dir/dmtools.jar" ]; then
            echo "$install_dir/dmtools.jar"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Check local build directory (development)
    if ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    # Check for any JAR file in the script directory
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 \( -name "dmtools*.jar" -o -name "*-all.jar" \) | head -1)
    # Check parent directory build folder (if script is in subdirectory)
    elif ls "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs"/*.jar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jar_file=$(find "$SCRIPT_DIR/../build/libs" -name "*-all.jar" | head -1)
    fi
    
    echo "$jar_file"
}

JAR_FILE=$(find_jar_file)

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
        chosen=$("$JAVA_CMD" -Dlog4j2.configurationFile=classpath:log4j2-cli.xml -Dlog4j.configuration=log4j2-cli.xml -Dlog4j2.disable.jmx=true -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED -XX:-PrintWarnings -Dpolyglot.engine.WarnInterpreterOnly=false -cp "$JAR_FILE" com.github.istin.dmtools.job.JobRunner interactive)
        if [ -n "$chosen" ]; then
            if [[ "$chosen" == run:* ]]; then
                target="${chosen#run:}"
                exec "$0" run "$target"
            else
                # chosen is "tool_name\tjson_params\toutput_format"
                tool_name="${chosen%%$'\t'*}"
                rest="${chosen#*$'\t'}"
                params="${rest%%$'\t'*}"
                output_format="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                if [ "$params" = "$rest" ]; then
                    output_format=""
                fi
                output_args=()
                if [ -n "$output_format" ]; then
                    output_args=("--output" "$output_format")
                fi
                if [ -n "$params" ] && [ "$tool_name" != "$params" ]; then
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" --data "$params" "${output_args[@]}"
                else
                    exec "$0" "$tool_name" "${output_args[@]}"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        exit 0
    else
        usage
    fi
    exit 0
fi

#!/bin/bash
# DMTools CLI Wrapper
# Usage: ./dmtools.sh [command] [args...]
# Supports: STDIN, heredoc, file input, inline JSON, and direct job-name execution for `run`

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

get_install_dir_candidates() {
    local script_parent_dir=""
    script_parent_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"

    if [ -n "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR"
    fi

    if [ -n "$script_parent_dir" ] && [ "$script_parent_dir" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$script_parent_dir"
    fi

    if [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "${DMTOOLS_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ] && [ "$HOME/.dmtools" != "$script_parent_dir" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$HOME/.dmtools"
    fi
}

# Find Java command (bundled or system)
find_java_command() {
    local install_dir=""
    while IFS= read -r install_dir; do
        [ -n "$install_dir" ] || continue

        # macOS has different JRE structure: Contents/Home/bin/java
        local bundled_java_macos="$install_dir/jre/Contents/Home/bin/java"
        local bundled_java="$install_dir/jre/bin/java"
        local bundled_java_exe="$install_dir/jre/bin/java.exe"

        # Check for bundled Java (order matters: macOS, Windows, Linux)
        if [ -x "$bundled_java_macos" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_macos"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java_exe" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java_exe"
            return 0
        elif [ -x "$bundled_java" ]; then
            echo "$bundled_java"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(get_install_dir_candidates)

    # Fall back to system Java
    if command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "java"
        return 0
    fi

    # No Java found
    return 1
}
